objective_for_doctor: A 37-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, a cough, and sensitive pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve been having a fever and a cough, and my throat really hurts—both tonsils hurt and my palate/pharynx feels sensitive and painful. I also have hoarseness, and the pain is about 7 out of 10.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—sorry you’re feeling so bad. How long has this been going on, and do you have any trouble swallowing, drooling, or shortness of breath?  
Doctor: Also, have you noticed a runny nose/cold symptoms or any swollen neck glands, and what’s the highest measured temperature?

It started recently—I’d say about the last few days, and I’ve had a cold about 2 weeks ago. I do have trouble because swallowing hurts, but I’m not drooling and I don’t feel short of breath.  

I also have cold symptoms like a cough, and I’ve had fever but I don’t know the exact highest temperature measurement. I’m not sure about swollen neck glands.

Doctor: Thanks—next questions: do you see white patches or pus on your tonsils, and do you have swollen/tender lymph nodes under your jaw or a bad-smelling breath? Also, any known exposure to strep/COVID/flu, or did symptoms start suddenly vs gradually?

I haven’t noticed any white patches or pus on my tonsils. I’m not sure about swollen or tender lymph nodes under my jaw, and I don’t know about bad-smelling breath.  

I don’t know of any specific exposure to strep, COVID, or flu, and it felt more gradual rather than suddenly starting.

Doctor: I hear you—since this is gradual over a few days with fever, cough, hoarseness, and no visible tonsillar exudate, I need to ask: do you have nasal congestion or a runny nose now, and are you currently able to swallow liquids (or is it mostly solids)? Also, have you had any significant body aches or headache?

Yes, I have nasal congestion/runny nose symptoms along with the cough. I can swallow liquids, but it hurts when I swallow.  

I’m not sure about significant body aches or headache—I haven’t really paid attention to that.

Doctor: I’m going to check for signs that point more toward viral URI vs strep—do you have any known exposure to someone with confirmed strep/“strep throat,” and do you have a distinct rash? Also, during the last day, has your cough been mostly dry or productive (with phlegm)?  
Doctor: For your exam, I’d like to look at your throat and neck—any visible swelling of the tonsils, and can you open wide so I can assess redness/ulcers?

I don’t know of any exposure to someone with confirmed strep. I don’t think I have a distinct rash.  

My cough is mostly dry, not much phlegm. And as for the throat exam, yes—go ahead and look; my tonsils and throat feel very sore.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—looking now: do your tonsils have any visible redness or ulcers, and are you feeling hoarse with a “voice change” more than throat-only pain?  
Doctor: Next, any shortness of breath, wheezing, or chest pain, and do you have measurable fever (even an estimate) since home?

My throat/tonsils look red and they feel very sore, but I don’t see ulcers. And yes, I’m hoarse—my voice feels changed, not just pain in my throat.  

No shortness of breath, no wheezing, and no chest pain. I’ve had fever, but I can’t measure it right now—just that I’ve been having fever at home.

Doctor: Based on the red, very sore throat with hoarseness and prominent runny/nasal symptoms plus a mostly dry cough (and no ulcers/exudate, no dyspnea, no chest pain), this sounds more like a viral upper-respiratory infection with laryngopharyngeal involvement than strep.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test (or throat culture if rapid is negative)
Okay, doctor. I’m okay with the rapid strep test (and throat culture if needed). Please go ahead.

REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test  
Doctor: While that’s pending, are you able to manage fluids and is your voice hoarseness improving or worsening over the last 24 hours?
Yes, I’m able to manage fluids, though it still hurts when I swallow. My hoarseness feels about the same to maybe a little worse over the last 24 hours.

Doctor: Thanks—since your hoarseness is persisting/worsening over 24 hours with a viral-type URI picture (runny nose, dry cough, red throat, no exudative ulcers), this fits viral laryngitis/pharyngitis; I want one more check: any severe one-sided throat pain, muffled “hot potato” voice, or neck swelling that makes turning your head hard?  
Doctor: Also, do you have asthma, immunosuppression, or are you a smoker/vaper?  
Doctor: If none of those are present and the rapid strep is negative, the diagnosis remains viral URI/laryngitis—recommend supportive care (fluids, acetaminophen/ibuprofen if safe, salt-water gargles, and voice rest) while awaiting the test.  

DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral laryngitis/pharyngitis (acute viral upper respiratory infection), pending negative rapid strep.
